title: error_invocation: .expect() invariant relies on jmap-types lock
description: error_invocation() calls serde_json::to_value(error).expect('JmapError::Serialize is infallible'). This is correct today because JmapError's Serialize impl never returns Err, but the invariant is cross-crate: if jmap-types ever adds a non-serializable variant, this becomes a runtime panic in jmap-server with no compile-time warning. The comment documents it, but no mechanism enforces it.
notes: Mitigation: (a) change signature to return Result<Invocation, ...> and propagate — but this changes public API, (b) keep .expect() but add a crate-level doc warning, (c) add a compile-time test in jmap-types that JmapError round-trips. Option (c) is best: add a test in jmap-types that serializes every JmapError variant.
